title: Automatic prompt engineering: using the LLM to generate prompts

videos.script: You have written a prompt, and it works. Is it the best one? {{works}} You would have to try others to know, and trying by hand is slow. {{slow}} Automatic prompt engineering hands that job to a program. {{program}} A model writes many candidate instructions. Each one is run on examples whose answers you already know. {{candidates}} Every candidate gets a score, and the best one is kept. {{score}} In this lesson you score five prompts against a tiny model, and the winner is not the one a person would pick. {{surprise}} The instruction a person would write first scores zero. Half a plain sentence scores full marks. {{zero}} Then comes the part that keeps the method honest. {{honest}} A score on the examples you chose it with says little. You test the winner on examples it has never seen. {{held}} And you read it, because a number cannot tell you what a prompt says. {{read}} This is the last lesson of the course, and it ends where good prompting starts: with a test. {{test}}
